corridor.lit_rule_definition: a coarse block is lit only if every fine cell in it is lit at that slice (block shadow fraction 0)
corridor.edge_rule: MOVE (r,c,t)->(r',c',t+d) with d = max(1, ceil(edge travel / slice)) as the planner counts it; both blocks lit and passable at every slice t..t+d; gates as astar_4d (passable, corner cut, step slope, cross-slope). WAIT (t->t+1) needs both voxels lit.
corridor.pruning: forward reach from the lit layer at slice 0 AND backward reach from the lit layer at the last slice: CMU's two-pass root / dead-end pruning, move-time aware

provenance.claim: Inside the corridor the model's shadow series never shows a dark block: SPICE Sun position + horizon cube (72 azimuth bins, two scales), coarse blocks, sampled slices. A statement about the model, not about the real surface.
provenance.uncertainty_note: B3: on 2027-05-30, 10.8 percent of cells are undecided lit/dark across NASA's 100 Site11 DEM clones (docs/research/dem_uncertainty_report.md); the corridor is only as certain as the DEM it was cast on.
provenance.reference: Otten, Jones, Wettergreen, Whittaker: Planning Routes of Continuous Illumination and Traversable Slope using Connected Component Analysis (ICRA 2015); Strategic Autonomy for Reducing Risk of Sun-Synchronous Lunar Polar Exploration (FSR 2017)
